runs.studyOutcome: Headline SURVIVED the recompute: still only 1 of 26 ZIPs (32505) covered by an FL064 E-5, still 12 of 26 above every Pensacola-side grade, and still only Destin and Gulf Breeze proper above every FL023 grade. Median monthly moved $2,599 -> $2,582; FL023 E-5 coverage 12 -> 11 of 26. New fifth finding replaces the old median-gap bullet: unincorporated Okaloosa levies 9.5165 mills against Escambia 13.4035 and Santa Rosa 11.3897, about $85/mo on a $330,000 home, which is why Valparaiso costs less per month than Cantonment despite a higher price.
runs.methodologyDecision: Modeled every ZIP at its county UNINCORPORATED rate rather than the research pack per-ZIP city assignments. The pack rated several high-impact assignments Low confidence, and the city-vs-unincorporated swing reaches 67% (City of Crestview 15.8751 vs unincorporated Okaloosa 9.5165) and 27% in Escambia. Publishing per-ZIP city guesses on a page that carries a Citing this study block would have been false precision. The unincorporated tier is the only High-confidence tier, is one consistent rule, and matches the page framing that these costs are a floor. City rates are disclosed in the simplifications so a reader can adjust.
openItems: Per-ZIP city/unincorporated assignment is unresolved and is the single biggest remaining uncertainty. Escambia PA parcel lookups on a sample of addresses per ZIP would settle 32503/32504/32505 (worth 3.6045 mills, 27% of the bill).
32561 spans three rates across two counties (Gulf Breeze city 11.2920, unincorporated Santa Rosa 11.3897, and Pensacola Beach in ESCAMBIA at 12.7185). Consider splitting or dropping that row.
Zillow typical values are still the July 2026 vintage; only the cost model was recomputed this run.

runs.method: Jurisdiction assigned from the Florida DOR 2026 preliminary certified NAL real property roll: all 407,635 parcels across Escambia, Santa Rosa and Okaloosa counted (not sampled), filtered to single-family use code 001, grouped by taxing authority and ZIP. Validated by resolving every taxing-authority code against a live parcel record by real address at each county appraiser, and cross-checked against 2020 Census block housing units joined to municipal boundaries (agrees within ~5 points on 24 of 26 ZIPs).
runs.outcome: 13 of 26 rows changed, 13 unchanged: the previous uniform-unincorporated model was already right for exactly half the set. Headline survived a second rebuild: still only 32505 covered by an FL064 E-5. No-grade FL064 went 12 -> 13, FL023 E-5 coverage 11 -> 10 of 26, median $2,582 -> $2,639.
runs.keyFinding: The prior run’s "Okaloosa is the cheap county" finding was wrong and has been replaced. Only 19.5% of Okaloosa single-family parcels actually pay the 9.5165 unincorporated rate; most populated unincorporated area sits in a fire-district MSTU at 11.79-12.27, and two of those districts (North Bay 11.7865, Florosa 11.9042) were missing from the millage table entirely. The new finding is that the city line matters more than the county line: 32502 inside Pensacola city limits pays $412/mo in tax on a $333,763 home while Pace pays $277 on a $330,382 home, $135/mo apart on a municipal boundary.
runs.blendedRows: 32536 Crestview (63% city / 37% county) at 13.5475 and 32578 Niceville (46% city / 54% split between North Bay and East Niceville FDs) at 12.8464, rather than a single city rate that would overstate them by $48 and $29 a month.
runs.caveatAdded: 32561 now carries an explicit caution: it splits ~60/40 between the City of Gulf Breeze and Pensacola Beach, which is in ESCAMBIA county, and Pensacola Beach land is leasehold on Santa Rosa Island rather than fee simple, so its ownership economics are not comparable to the rest of the table.
